rule: GOAL: Arrange the four colored tiles below to perfectly match the sequence shown at the top. CONTROLS: Click a tile to select it, then click a target slot to place it. RULE: Tiles swap positions; the empty gray spot moves to the original location. TRAP: Thinking you must drag tiles; they only move via click-to-select, click-to-place.

GOAL: Move the square to the far end of the diagonal path. CONTROLS: Click on the grid to jump the square to a new position. RULE: You can only move exactly six steps along the diagonal line. TRAP: Thinking you could click any dot to land; odd-step distances are blocked.

GOAL: Navigate from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner using the fewest moves possible. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character two spaces in that direction, skipping the tile in between. RULE: You can only jump if both the skipped tile and the landing spot are open floor. TRAP: Believing you can stop early; if the two-space jump is blocked, you do not move at all.

GOAL: Place three boxes into the designated slots along the horizontal bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; Space picks up or drops the carried box. RULE: You can only carry one box at a time, requiring you to shuttle back and forth. TRAP: Trying to push boxes into place instead of carrying them wastes moves and causes jams.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the socket using five slots. CONTROLS: Click dashes to activate slots; click stems to change direction; click the ball to launch. RULE: An active slot with a stem moves the ball down; without a stem, it moves left. TRAP: Assuming slot position determines direction, when only the stem state actually controls the path.

GOAL: Pour liquid onto the bar to fill the target zones below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the spout horizontally; spacebar releases the liquid. RULE: Liquid spreads sideways when it hits a solid surface, then flows off the edges. TRAP: Assuming liquid stays in a single column ignores how it widens upon impact, causing missed targets.

GOAL: Move the yellow plug to close the gap against the wall. CONTROLS: Clicking blue blocks shifts the plug right and adjusts the boundary edges. RULE: The plug’s edge must align perfectly with the moving white boundary to win. TRAP: Thinking any click moves the plug; only clicking the blue blocks triggers movement.

GOAL: Solve a five-piece color cycle to match every slot to its required hue. CONTROLS: Click to pick up a piece, click again to drop it onto another slot. RULE: Dropping a piece onto an occupied slot swaps the two pieces instantly. TRAP: Believing you need empty slots to move pieces; the swap mechanic lets you rotate the entire cycle without gaps.

GOAL: Place seven symbols in nested colored boxes to match a target sequence. CONTROLS: Click slots to assign symbols, click palette to select, press space to validate. RULE: Traverse main row left-to-right; at connectors, enter sub-box, fill it, then return to continue main row. TRAP: Assuming strict left-to-right across all boxes; nesting resets order, requiring you to finish inner paths before exiting.

GOAL: Arrange scattered items into two distinct boxes to form a complete chain. CONTROLS: Click a piece to pick it up, then click a slot to drop it; press space to verify. RULE: Pieces must be placed in specific slots to link the red and green sections correctly. TRAP: Assuming the connector draws a visible stem immediately; it may only appear or validate after all pieces are placed.

GOAL: Fill the grid so a single path reads the target color sequence. CONTROLS: Click a palette piece, then click a slot to place it. Press space to test. RULE: The path visits all slots in order; matching repeated color blocks reveals hidden connector positions. TRAP: Assuming connectors only link adjacent colors; they actually bridge gaps to repeat the entire color pattern.

GOAL: Match the target sequence by ordering three colored sub-boxes. CONTROLS: Click connectors to set traversal order; click letters to fill box slots; spacebar confirms the solution. RULE: The connector’s color dictates which sub-box is read first, second, and third. TRAP: Assuming fixed box order causes mismatch; the connectors determine the sequence, not physical position.

GOAL: Match a hidden color chain by nesting boxes through connectors. CONTROLS: Drag pieces to slots; Space submits. RULE: A connector placed in a box slot links to the box of that color, exposing its slots. TRAP: Assuming slots are independent. Ignoring that connectors hide or reveal other slots breaks the sequence.

GOAL: Slide the object left until its body covers the gap. CONTROLS: Click right to move the object; click left to adjust the band. RULE: The object’s full width, not just the tab, must overlap the gap. TRAP: Thinking only the tab needed to touch the gap wasted time on alignment.

GOAL: Align five glyph slots to their specific rotated targets to clear the level. CONTROLS: Use arrows to move the cursor between slots and cycle through glyph variations. RULE: Each slot requires the unique rotation present in its bank, not just any valid symmetry. TRAP: Assuming any symmetric match works wastes actions; only the exact bank-listed rotation counts.

GOAL: Merge two separate pieces into a single shape to win. CONTROLS: Clicking the map sets a target that pulls nearby pieces toward it. RULE: When two pieces share the same target, they merge into a larger block. TRAP: Assuming you must move pieces individually; letting them converge on one spot saves actions.

ESTABLISHED: The ink block drifts left two columns per commit. Manual arrow keys move the block independently of this drift. FAILED: Manually pushing the block into the barrel neck at column 23 caused no reaction. Assuming the block width remains constant failed. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the leftmost barrel wall or the neck entrance with the current 4-pixel block state. CONTROLS: Commit advances the block left. Arrow keys reposition the block. The block shrinks to 2x2 pixels on odd commits.

GOAL: Prime the syringe by pushing the ink block into the narrow neck. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the ink block left or right within the barrel. RULE: Only the two-pixel-tall ink state fits through the neck; the four-pixel-tall state is too wide. TRAP: Believing the ink drifts left automatically on its own, rather than requiring manual movement to reach the neck.

ESTABLISHED: The dot indicates a block is currently on the wire; the legend is a live status display. The red block is frozen at rows 13-16 because the wire cannot reach that height. FAILED: Dragging the red block to column 18 and retracting the wire did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply getting all three blocks to touch the handle, as they are physically blocked by the handle’s right edge. CONTROLS: UP moves the handle vertically along the track; RIGHT extends the wire through blocks; LEFT retracts the wire and drags blocks.

GOAL: Extend colored plugs to cover matching target crosses. CONTROLS: Click bracket-shaped glyphs to extend or retract the adjacent plug line. RULE: The glyph opening toward the plug’s cap extends it; the one facing the tip retracts it. TRAP: Assuming both brackets perform the same action; clicking the wrong one shrinks the plug instead of growing it.

GOAL: Lift the ink block up the barrel until it touches the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; printing shrinks it and pumps it upward. RULE: A full ink block is too wide to fit under the handle, so you must shrink it first. TRAP: Believing the block only moves when you press arrows; printing actually drives the upward progress.

GOAL: Reach the green exit while navigating a corridor guarded by a charging enemy. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; the enemy charges two tiles toward the player's row. RULE: The enemy only moves horizontally, leaving vertical paths safe during its turn. TRAP: Believing the enemy blocks all paths; moving vertically avoids its horizontal charge entirely.

GOAL: Deliver two distinct shapes to specific circular zones. CONTROLS: Clicking a point pulls the nearest shape toward it in fixed steps. RULE: Each click moves a shape exactly six units diagonally or orthogonally. TRAP: Assuming one click suffices for large distances; long paths require multiple hops.

GOAL: Route the liquid stream through three specific horizontal bars to fill their designated exit pockets without spilling onto other surfaces. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the active bar horizontally; clicking a bar makes it active; the spacebar initiates the liquid flow. RULE: The liquid only flows into the pockets directly aligned with the bar's open ends, so precise horizontal alignment is critical. TRAP: Assuming the liquid flows from the top down; it actually rises from below, requiring you to position bars to catch upward streams.

GOAL: Align two cross-shaped tools so their arms cover all target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches which cross is active. RULE: Only the selected cross moves, so you must toggle between them to position each correctly. TRAP: Assuming both crosses move simultaneously or that you can drag them together wastes actions.

GOAL: Reach the exit while safely removing a charging enemy blocking your path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile at a time on the grid. RULE: Land directly on an enemy to destroy it; never stand in its row unless attacking. TRAP: Entering the enemy’s row without attacking triggers a fatal charge; approach from a different row first.

GOAL: Move each colored shape so its outline covers all matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: Shapes must align perfectly with their target dots to clear the level. TRAP: Moving shapes in random order wastes actions; solve them sequentially to save moves.

GOAL: Align the bottom edge of each colored band precisely with its matching gap row. CONTROLS: Click a band to shift it up or down; click a wall to move it left or right. RULE: A gap is cleared only when the band’s end touches the gap’s far side, not just the near edge. TRAP: Assuming any overlap with the gap row works; precise alignment with the far column is required.

GOAL: Park the box in the top-left corner within four moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character and drag the attached box. RULE: The box stays directly below you while moving left or right. TRAP: Believing you can grab a second box while carrying one.

GOAL: Align three separate shapes to cover all red dots within the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active shape three pixels per press; Space switched to the next shape. RULE: Each directional input shifts the shape by three units, so divide pixel distance by three for presses. TRAP: Assuming arrow presses equal single pixel steps caused overshooting; always calculate moves in threes.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow block sits inside the yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Red clicks rotate the ring one step backward; green clicks rotate it forward. RULE: Each click shifts every block one position, keeping the bracket fixed in place. TRAP: Thinking the bracket moves with the blocks, causing you to miss the fixed target slot.

GOAL: Guide the sprite to the blue shape at the end of the corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the sprite one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Stepping on the plus symbol mirrors the shape in the bottom-left indicator. TRAP: Assuming the goal is to match the indicator or push the plus into the box.

GOAL: Place the purple square inside the dashed ring. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot moves the white diamond there, swapping with any object already at that location. RULE: The purple square moves exactly half the distance between the white and gray diamonds. TRAP: Assuming the white diamond itself needed to reach the ring, ignoring the square’s specific positioning requirement.

GOAL: Match the panel’s big grid to the mini pattern by turning specific blocks red. CONTROLS: Click a block to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: The central mini display shows the exact target arrangement of red blocks. TRAP: Assuming the mini display is just a legend; it actually dictates the required solution.

GOAL: Paint specific blocks orange to match the two target patterns shown in the mini displays. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to change their color from blue to the target orange. RULE: Each mini display reveals the required pattern for its corresponding three-by-three section of the grid. TRAP: Assuming the mini centers are paintable targets rather than fixed display indicators.

GOAL: Place both charcoal blocks into the dark ring sockets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicks change which block is selected. RULE: The white dot marks the active block, so click to target the correct piece before moving. TRAP: Assuming arrows move a fixed block wastes time; selection must be manually switched to control the other piece.

GOAL: Clear the board by capturing tokens until only one remains. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it, then click the highlighted landing spot to jump over an adjacent opponent. RULE: You capture by jumping directly over a neighbor into an empty space, removing the jumped piece. TRAP: Assuming a piece is trapped because it looks isolated, when it actually has a valid jump path into a gap created by a previous capture.

GOAL: Move two shapes to cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches between the plus and the X. RULE: A shape changes color only when its center touches a matching swatch. TRAP: Assuming the color persists if you move away; the shape reverts to its original color if the center leaves the swatch.

GOAL: Move both blue squares into the top bar of the maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide one square until it hits a wall or another square. RULE: Squares stop only when blocked; they do not stop at empty spaces. TRAP: Thinking adjacent squares merge or win; they remain separate and must reach specific target cells.

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells to match the shapes held by orange markers. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell changes its color; clicking a marker reveals its shape. RULE: Only cells covered by orange markers need to be painted; red markers indicate correct colors. TRAP: Assuming red markers also required painting wasted time on cells that were already correct.

GOAL: Guide two yellow tokens to the bracketed corners. CONTROLS: Click arrows to shift rows or the outer perimeter. RULE: Red arrows shift left or up; green arrows shift right or down. TRAP: Assuming all arrows rotate the same way wastes moves; directions oppose each other.

GOAL: Move yellow to the left target and orange to the right target by rotating two interlocking rings. CONTROLS: Red buttons rotate rings forward; green buttons rotate rings backward. RULE: The rings share two slots, so rotating one moves items between them, but rotations do not cancel out if the order is wrong. TRAP: Assuming left and right rotations commute; they do not, so repeating a sequence does not reset the shared slots.

GOAL: Move the handle to the orange chain to capture the remaining targets. CONTROLS: Clicking a target swaps the handle with the nearest object in that chain. RULE: The handle only travels along connected paths of its current color. TRAP: Assuming a single global handle; you must manually switch chains to reach all groups.

GOAL: Match the target color pattern by cycling tiles through blue, red, and orange states. CONTROLS: Left-click advances a tile’s color one step in the fixed cycle: blue to red, then to orange, then back to blue. RULE: Each tile requires a specific number of clicks to reach its target color, with orange needing two clicks from blue. TRAP: Assuming tiles cycle directly from red to blue, which causes extra clicks when orange is the required final state.

GOAL: Overlap both squares into the single same cell to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Victory triggers only when both pieces occupy the exact same coordinate. TRAP: Assuming reaching the top row wins; moving both up there does not end the level.

GOAL: Place three boxes into matching sockets. CONTROLS: Click to select, arrows to move. RULE: Active boxes push others; some warp on impact. TRAP: Assuming all boxes move normally. One warped far away, requiring repositioning before seating.

ESTABLISHED: The player is a five-by-five square. White cells are solid walls. A heavy block rests on a floor plate. FAILED: Moving the player onto the plate failed to open any path. Pressing the action button did not shrink the player or change the active form. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing the block to the target spot. The block is not a door that opens when pushed. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the five-by-five square. The action button toggles a state but leaves the player’s size and position unchanged.

GOAL: Align the plug’s prongs with the pins, then slide it right until the tips meet the pins to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug three cells per press. RULE: The plug stops immediately when its prongs touch the pins, signaling a successful connection. TRAP: Believing you must force the prongs through or overlap the pins wastes time; simple adjacency is sufficient to win.

GOAL: Transform three specific toggle cells to pink while matching the surrounding pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a standard cell flips it. Clicking a toggle cell flips itself and its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Toggle cells must be pink, forcing you to click them despite the messy side effects. TRAP: Believing toggles are obstacles to be avoided. Skipping them prevents completion; you must embrace the chaos they create to satisfy the color requirement.

GOAL: Move two tokens to their target cells using minimal clicks. CONTROLS: Green buttons shift rows or columns; red buttons attempt reversals. RULE: Only the play area changes matter; ignore the shrinking budget bar when checking states. TRAP: Assuming red buttons perfectly reverse greens caused wasted steps verifying against misleading HUD data.

GOAL: Slide the black piece so its mirror reflection aligns perfectly with the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black piece three grid cells per press in that direction. RULE: The charcoal piece mirrors the black piece’s position across the vertical center line. TRAP: Assuming moves slide until blocked; they actually stop exactly after three cells.

GOAL: Move the white marker to the purple ring center in five steps. CONTROLS: Clicking a square moves the marker; clicking the black anchor swaps their positions. RULE: The midpoint between start and end must land on a valid, unobstructed grid cell. TRAP: Assuming the final destination itself needs to be clear; only the path midpoint matters for validity.

GOAL: Place the two yellow blocks into the marked bracket slots. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shift the row; up and down arrows cycle the vertical column. RULE: Blocks move as a unit; the row shifts horizontally while the column wraps vertically. TRAP: Treating blocks as independent causes chaos; they are locked together, so plan the group's path, not individual stops.

GOAL: Align the moving shadow with the yellow target to complete the reflection. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space switches focus between the divider and the piece. RULE: The divider acts as a mirror line; moving it shifts the reflection axis, while moving the piece changes the source position. TRAP: Assuming the divider is static; it must be moved first to position the mirror axis correctly before aligning the piece.

GOAL: Guide the knob to the exit by managing block positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks toggle block visibility. RULE: Toggling a block off reveals the path underneath; the knob can only occupy visible cells. TRAP: Assuming the knob leaves a permanent trail. It does not; moving away simply reveals the static background color of that cell.

GOAL: Dissolve the valve cap by printing its pattern, then shove the ink block into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ink block; pressing against the cap pattern consumes it to open the path. RULE: The block must fully merge with the handle, not just touch its edge, to clear the level. TRAP: Stopping when the block first aligns with the channel wastes time; you must force a full overlap.

GOAL: Move the T and L pieces onto the bottom yellow targets, then raise the divider so their shadows perfectly cover the top yellow shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object or the divider; Space cycles selection between the divider, L piece, and T piece. RULE: Shadows project vertically from pieces against the divider line; raising the divider shortens shadows to match the upper targets. TRAP: Moving the T piece down before shifting it left causes a collision with the stationary L piece; always move left first.

GOAL: Paint the top half white by positioning the plunger upright above the canvas. CONTROLS: Arrows move and rotate the plunger; clicks select colors; space stamps the paint. RULE: The plunger’s edge defines a line through the center; only the canvas side touching the plunger gets painted. TRAP: Assuming tilt angles arbitrarily change the painted area, rather than realizing position relative to the center dictates which half receives the color.

GOAL: Align three diamond chains to their target rings. CONTROLS: Click to move the active diamond; click an empty cell to transfer the handle to a new chain. RULE: A chain’s total value equals its diamond count multiplied by its current ring target. TRAP: Assuming the transferred diamond increases the chain’s count; it replaces an anchor, keeping the total fixed.

GOAL: Paint the canvas's top rows purple and bottom rows orange using the plunger. CONTROLS: Space paints, mouse selects color, Left/Right tilts, Down drops the plunger. RULE: The plunger only falls when tilted, sliding to a specific edge-aligned position. TRAP: Pressing Down while upright does nothing; you must tilt first to drop it.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking blocks opens vertical channels through solid walls. The player floats upward through cleared paths, stopping at the first solid ceiling. FAILED: Staying low or moving sideways without clearing the overhead block yields no progress. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the surface of the water or staying in the lower chambers. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks destroy blocks. Left moves left. The player rises automatically when the path above is clear.

GOAL: Clear the vertical channel and rise to the top of the level. CONTROLS: Clicks removed blocking green blocks; left arrows shifted the player into the cleared path. RULE: Removing blocks above the player creates an open shaft for immediate upward movement. TRAP: Assuming blocks only clear their own row; destroying one block often opens multiple rows, allowing a single shift to trigger a massive ascent.

GOAL: Guide the knob through pink and red columns to reach the yellow base at the top. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move the knob up, down, left, and right across the grid. RULE: The knob only moves on open paths defined by the active colored columns, requiring precise alignment. TRAP: Assuming you can turn corners at any height; you must reach the specific row where the pink and red paths overlap to switch columns.

GOAL: Route water streams to fill specific pockets while managing overflow. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks select bars; arrow keys slide them horizontally; space pours water. RULE: Bars must align to catch incoming streams and direct exits into target zones. TRAP: Assuming edge-flush bars absorb off-board flow; they often create unmanageable streams.

GOAL: Lift the divider to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space cycles selection. RULE: Only unlocked pieces move; seated blocks stay fixed. TRAP: Assuming all blocks are movable wastes turns on locked pieces.

GOAL: Paint specific grid halves using rotated stamps and a solid block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plunger; clicks select colors; SPACE stamps the current pose. RULE: Each plunger position defines a unique diagonal or horizontal cut line for the stamp. TRAP: Assuming one diagonal stamp covers all needed colors; you must reposition for each distinct half.

GOAL: Fit the blue and green pieces into their matching sockets to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; the spacebar rotated it; clicking selected a new piece. RULE: Shapes only fit when their protrusions align perfectly with the empty holes in the target shape. TRAP: Assuming rotation was needed for the blue piece wasted time, as it only required a straight translation.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding a bouncing orange and destroying a red guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; the orange moves automatically each turn. RULE: The orange bounces off walls and reverses direction, creating a predictable patrol pattern. TRAP: Assuming the orange stays still; ignoring its constant movement leads to fatal collisions.

GOAL: Place the knob on the purple pedestal to collect the fourth key. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the character; clicks toggled color states to alter terrain solidity. RULE: Standing on a teleport knob while a specific color is active swapped its location to the paired pedestal. TRAP: Assuming the knob stayed put; it vanished from the top-left and reappeared at the bottom-left after activation.

GOAL: Guide dots to dead ends, then align squares to overlap them. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active dot or square; clicks switch active dots or activate squares. RULE: Only the selected element moves; others freeze until clicked again. TRAP: Moving dots before positioning squares wastes turns; park dots first, then solve the square alignment.

GOAL: Seat two crosses in their rings and park the box. CONTROLS: Arrows push the box; pushing a cross seats it. RULE: Crosses block the box; use them as walls or targets. TRAP: Moving the box early traps it against cross arms; push crosses first.

GOAL: Adjust the grid dividers to frame the piece in the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected item; Space cycles focus between the piece and the two dividers. RULE: Dividers shift only when selected; move them into position before guiding the piece. TRAP: Moving the piece too early locks it in place, wasting actions needed to adjust the frame.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding patrolling enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per press. RULE: Enemies follow fixed, predictable paths; timing your moves around their loops is key. TRAP: Assuming the direct route is safe; you must take the long way to avoid deadly patrols.

GOAL: Clear the level by forcing two squares into the same cell to trigger a win. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then use arrow keys to move it. RULE: Moving one square in a direction moves the other square in the opposite direction. TRAP: Forgetting that selecting a new piece cancels the previous selection, causing unintended moves.

GOAL: Clear the path by eliminating red enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character. RULE: Stepping onto a red enemy destroys it. TRAP: Assuming enemies move or attack independently; they are static hazards until touched.

GOAL: Move the yellow tokens from the middle ring to the outer ring slots. CONTROLS: One button shifts tokens outward to the next ring; the other moves them one step clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Outward shifts keep the same slot position, while steps change the position index within the ring. TRAP: Assuming outward moves change the slot position leads to wasted clicks; the position only changes with the step control.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with specific color patterns by positioning a plunger and selecting swatches. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plunger to different zones; mouse clicks select colors or activate stamps. RULE: Each plunger position corresponds to a unique geometric region that gets painted with the selected color. TRAP: Assuming all stamp regions are pre-verified; untested zones may behave unexpectedly, requiring careful step-by-step confirmation.

GOAL: Guide two yellow markers to specific numbered slots on a rotating track. CONTROLS: Press Down to shift both markers forward one step; press Up to lift one marker into a holding loop, and Down again to drop it back. RULE: Lifting a marker removes it from the active track, allowing you to shift the other marker independently to adjust their relative distance. TRAP: Believing you must move both markers simultaneously to align them wastes moves; you must isolate one marker to set the correct gap.

GOAL: Collect all red dots by moving shapes to reveal hidden items beneath them. CONTROLS: Space toggled the current shape; arrow keys moved the selected shape across the grid. RULE: Dots were invisible under shapes, requiring you to move objects away to expose them. TRAP: Assuming all visible dots were complete, missing the red dot hidden under the plus sign.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with specific colored patterns using a movable plunger. CONTROLS: Click swatches to select colors; press Space to stamp the current pose; arrow keys reposition the plunger. RULE: Each pose applies a unique geometric mask, so precise positioning determines which cells get painted. TRAP: Believing navigation is free; failing to verify the plunger’s exact pose before stamping causes irreversible errors.

GOAL: Guide two squares to their respective target plates without blocking each other. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected square one grid step in that direction. RULE: Squares must land on matching colored plates to open gates for the other square. TRAP: Mistaking the square’s starting position for a wall blocks movement; treat occupied cells as open floor.

ESTABLISHED: Three pieces exist. Each has two protrusions. All six protrusions must connect in pairs between different pieces. No loose ends remain. FAILED: Moving pieces to overlap single prongs while leaving others unconnected. Ignoring the requirement that every single prong finds exactly one partner. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching pieces or creating a single joint. Partial connections where one prong floats freely do not count. CONTROLS: Directional keys move selected pieces. Selecting a piece and moving it changes its position relative to others.

GOAL: Place two pieces and two dividers to fill the yellow target zone with their reflections. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected item; Space cycles through pieces and dividers. RULE: Dividers act as mirrors; moving them shifts the reflection of the pieces across that axis. TRAP: Believing dividers are solid walls. They are permeable; pieces and dividers can cross each other without blocking.

GOAL: Route liquid to all four cups without spilling. CONTROLS: Click to select a bar, arrow keys to move it, space to pour. RULE: Liquid flows through gaps, not through solid bars. TRAP: Assuming top bars block bottom exits; they only block if directly overlapping the flow path.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the chaser. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step per turn. RULE: The chaser always moves toward your position after you move. TRAP: Assuming the chaser can pass through blocked tiles to cut you off.

GOAL: Guide the knob to the yellow base. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks pump the gray square to change bar colors. RULE: Pumping converts blue segments to walkable white ones on the bottom bar. TRAP: Assuming a tight action budget led to over-planning; the actual limit was generous.

GOAL: Float the plug to a surface gap by balancing liquid levels across connected bands. CONTROLS: Click pumps to transfer liquid between bands; click gates to move the plug. RULE: The plug floats on the surface, so its height matches the liquid level in its current band. TRAP: Assuming a gate click changes liquid volume; it only moves the plug, requiring pumps to adjust levels afterward.

ESTABLISHED: The crown destroys overlapping shapes, leaving only a 2x2 remnant. FAILED: Moving pieces blindly triggers the crown’s attack, destroying progress. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching the bubble, as the crown likely blocks entry or attacks nearby. CONTROLS: Clicking moves a piece toward the target; the crown attacks on contact, not on command.

GOAL: Fit the cross into the ring and box into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows push the selected piece until it hits a wall or another piece. RULE: Pieces stop only when blocked; empty space is always traversable. TRAP: Thinking you can stop mid-slide; you must plan routes where collisions define the final position.

GOAL: Align each slot’s glyph to the expected letter from the derived sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP rotates the current glyph’s letter value. RULE: A slot is correct only when its glyph’s letter matches the target sequence. TRAP: Assuming a glyph’s visual shape was fixed; ignoring rotation meant missing valid letter matches.

GOAL: Clear the board by shrinking specific colored chains to fit within the remaining space. CONTROLS: Clicking a color shrinks its front segment; clicking a different color grows it, pushing connected neighbors away. RULE: Growth pushes attached chains, but shrinking only removes the front tip without moving others, allowing you to untangle overlapping stacks. TRAP: Assuming growth pushes all connected colors equally; it only pushes the chain physically attached to the growing tip’s front.

GOAL: Position the ink block so the blue segment sits on the left before printing. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ink stack; clicks load patterns and trigger the valve. RULE: The print mechanism only accepts the ink if the blue part is the leftmost column. TRAP: Thinking any arrangement works if you just press the final button; wrong alignment jams the machine.

ESTABLISHED: Moves are world-relative, not local. Codes {d1,s1} and {d0,s0,s1} both move left 8. {d0,s0} moves down 4. Rotation 180 does not invert vertical movement direction. FAILED: Local-frame rotation hypothesis. Testing specific bit combinations for "up" movement yielded no row decrease. GOAL IS NOT: A rotation-dependent movement system where "down" becomes "up" at 180 degrees. CONTROLS: Input bits map to world directions. Left is confirmed. Up is unconfirmed or blocked. Right and Down are partially mapped but inconsistent with rotation assumptions.

ESTABLISHED: The bubble floats in the lower pool. Flower chambers exist above and below, connected by narrow water channels. Solid black boundaries cap the visible world at the top and bottom edges. FAILED: Searching visible coordinates for a plus sign yielded nothing. Attempting to locate the goal within the current screen boundaries failed. GOAL IS NOT: A visible plus sign within the current view. The objective is not currently on-screen in the standard water pools. CONTROLS: The bubble moves with water currents. It rises to ceilings and sinks with water levels, but cannot break solid black

GOAL: Route colored plugs to matching sockets by sliding walls to open gates and set extension lengths. CONTROLS: Click pairs of wall edges to shift adjacent segments, changing their lengths and alignment. RULE: Gates only open when neighboring wall lengths match exactly, allowing plugs to pass through. TRAP: Assuming walls can be adjusted freely; ignoring minimum length limits and gate synchronization caused repeated dead ends.

GOAL: Slide the room to the board and click the token to capture it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the room; clicks select and place tokens. RULE: Capture only happens when the room is fully plugged into the board’s edge. TRAP: Ignoring shake animations made you think moves succeeded when they were blocked, wasting time on phantom progress.

GOAL: Rotate seven glyph slots to match a target sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; pressing up advances the current slot's glyph. RULE: Each press cycles the glyph forward by one position in a fixed seven-item loop. TRAP: Assuming slots share a global state; each slot has an independent rotation cycle.

ESTABLISHED: O autonomously grabs and places boxes on rows 12 and 32. Dropping boxes elsewhere is rejected or blocked. FAILED: Forcing boxes into wall slots outside rows 12 and 32. Carrying boxes to non-slot wall columns. GOAL IS NOT: Placing boxes on any wall cell. The wall only accepts boxes at specific row slots. CONTROLS: Movement carries attached boxes. Space drops the carried box. Walls block movement if not a valid slot.
GOAL: Slide the box into the ring’s center. CONTROLS: Arrows move the box. RULE: The ring is a visual target, not a wall. TRAP: Avoiding the ring outline wastes moves; drive straight through.

GOAL: Guide the Y-shape into the bubble while dodging the crown. CONTROLS: Clicking a square moves the Y toward that location. RULE: Moving pieces are immune to the crown’s attacks, allowing safe passage through danger zones. TRAP: Believing you must detour around the crown wastes time; direct paths through its area are often safe.

GOAL: Guide the target block down into the floor gap to escape. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle dash or stem bits, setting direction and distance. RULE: The active piece moves only if its shape matches the instruction’s bit pattern. TRAP: Assuming the arch moves with the target; only the target responds to commands.

GOAL: Navigate the block through the gap and into the arch cavity above. CONTROLS: Click dashes to move up, stems to move right, and the blue ball to execute. RULE: The block moves only when the run button is pressed, not during setup. TRAP: Assuming immediate movement after toggling switches wastes clicks; always verify the full sequence before running.

ESTABLISHED: The drain rate is strictly two bar segments per move, and the total path distance exceeds the bar's capacity by two segments. FAILED: Assuming the sprite footprint allows diagonal shortcuts or that the drain rate varies with remaining lives. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the exit within the initial bar charge without utilizing intermediate refills. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the sprite five units; successful moves consume bar segments; touching refill stations restores the full bar.

GOAL: Match all seven rotating glyphs to the bank patterns by identifying their true rotation classes. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selection cursor; pressing up or down cycled the current glyph through the seven bank variations. RULE: A glyph is solved only if it matches a bank pattern via rotation, not just visual similarity or pixel count. TRAP: Assuming a glyph with an empty center row belonged to the same class as another empty-row glyph, ignoring column alignment differences.

GOAL: Thread the wire tip through the block chain. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the wire tip, dragging connected blocks along. RULE: Pushing one block shifts the entire connected row, provided space allows. TRAP: Assuming the tip must reach the far edge; it only needs to align with the target band.

GOAL: Collect rings and reach the exit before the energy bar empties. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; moving onto a plus sign refills energy. RULE: You must grab both rings to open the exit gate. TRAP: Ignoring the energy bar causes a game over; always prioritize refilling over immediate exit.

GOAL: Guide the character through the maze to the exit point. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Pressing the spacebar toggles a mode that retracts obstacles, allowing passage through blocked paths. TRAP: Do not assume obstacles remain blocked; the toggle state persists even when you move away from the switch.

GOAL: Guide the retractable wire tip to the designated target zone by extending or retracting it to specific grid positions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys extend or retract the wire tip along the horizontal axis. RULE: The wire tip moves in discrete six-unit steps, but the initial position is a unique fifteen-unit stub that jumps to sixteen on the first extension. TRAP: Assuming the initial position follows the standard six-unit grid pattern causes off-by-one errors in predicting block collisions.

GOAL: Reach the exit while keeping the legend blue. CONTROLS: Arrows move and push blocks. Entering the prism toggles the legend color. RULE: The legend must be blue when entering the exit. TRAP: Stepping on the prism again turns the legend orange, forcing a long detour to avoid it.
